title: Orchestrate notarize + rolling promotion for model artifacts and perf profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Implement a CI pipeline stage that notarizes model build artifacts and performance profiles, then performs a controlled, rolling promotion to the 'pinned' catalog. This pipeline must produce verifiable provenance, produce signed artifacts compatible with our runtime, and support staged rollouts (canary -> 25% -> 100%), with automatic rollback on quality regressions. Scope: - Build step produces model.tar.gz, metadata.json, and perf_profile.pb - Notarization uses cosign for container-like artifacts and a detached sig for raw blobs; store signatures and provenance in the artifact catalog (s3://redwood-artifacts/provenance/) - Publish perf profiles alongside artifacts and generate machine-readable metadata for Console and runtime to consume - Promotion workflow: ci -> canary (runtime routing rules) -> gradual pin -> full pin - Integrations: GitHub Actions (or internal CI), Artifact Catalog service, Console rollouts API, observability dashboard for profile regressions Trade-offs considered: - We prefer cosign for standardization, but raw blob signing required a small wrapper to support detached signatures; this increases pipeline complexity. - Staging in S3 will duplicate storage for a short window (build artifacts + promoted copies) but simplifies atomic swap semantics for pinning. - Rolling promotion will rely on runtime routing for gradual traffic shifts; more complex but avoids multiple model versions in serving pools. Non-goals: provisioning Dedicated capacity or change to kernel selection logic.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces signed artifacts and stores signatures in the provenance bucket with a stable layout
Perf profiles are published with metadata and linked to the artifact ID
A single pipeline run can trigger a canary promotion and move through 25%/100% stages via rollout API
Automatic rollback triggers when perf regression alert threshold is exceeded
All produced artifacts are verifiable using the documented cosign/gpg commands in the onboarding playbook
comments: 2025-01-09 - Kickoff: aligned on artifact layout and signing approach. Action: JoseF to prototype cosign detached signature wrapper. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Onboard+Notarization+Design)

2025-01-15 - Prototype review: cosign wrapper works for model.tar.gz but requires deterministic build step to avoid signature churn. Decision: pin build container image digest and record build args in metadata.json.
2025-01-20 - Security review session: agreed to add an HSM-backed key rotation plan; short-term use of KMS with restricted service account. Follow-up: create ENG-20890 to codify key rotation.

2025-01-28 - PR opened for pipeline changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/12873 (adds GitHub Action 'notarize-and-promote'). Requested changes: improve retry logic on S3 put and surface failure reasons in CI logs.
2025-02-04 - Observability stub: added dashboard panel for 'profile regression alerts' (Grafana: /d/kv123/profile-regressions). Need to wire alert -> rollback lambda. Assigned to Priya.

2025-02-11 - Integration test run: successfully signed and promoted a test model to canary; observed a latency spike during canary. Decision: reduce initial canary traffic to 5% until KV cache warms. Follow-up task created: ENG-20902.
2025-02-14 - Review: PM and Design approved rollout copy in Console and added link to rollout settings in PR UI. Pending: final sign-off on HSM integration plan.
implementation_notes: Use deterministic packaging: sort files, strip timestamps, and use reproducible tar settings to reduce signature churn
Promotion job will write a 'pin' record to Catalog service (POST /v1/catalog/pins) containing artifact-id, release-tag, and rollout plan
Rollback handler will call Catalog to unpin and instruct Router to route back to previous pinned version
Add end-to-end test that validates cosign signature verification: 'cosign verify-blob --keyring <public> <artifact>'
